Pairs to Ten Rules

Cross out pairs of digits until none is left.

The rules

The field
Digits 1 to 9 in nine columns, read row by row like a text.
Pairs
Two digits are crossed out together when they are equal (3 and 3) or add up to 10 (1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5).
Seeing each other
The two must see each other: next to each other across, down or diagonally, or with only crossed-out cells between them on that line. Across also runs over the end of a row: the last digit of a row sees the first of the next one, and so on in reading order.
Add
When you are stuck, tap Add: all digits not yet crossed out are written again, in the same order, at the end of the field. At most 5 times per game.
Empty rows
A row whose nine cells are all crossed out vanishes.
Winning and losing
You win when every digit is crossed out. You lose when no pair is left and no Add either, or when the field grows to more than 40 rows.
Start
Classic: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9, then 1 1 1 2 1 3 1 4 1 5 1 6 1 7 1 8 1 9 (the numbers 1 to 19 without 10). Random: three, four or five rows; the easier the level, the more pairs stand right next to each other.
Help
Undo goes back any number of steps. Hint marks a pair that can be crossed out, or says that only Add is left.

Example

The classic start. The 1 at the top left and the 1 below it see each other (down) and are equal. The 9 at the end of the first row and the 1 at the start of the second see each other over the end of the row and add up to 10.
